                         num_tasks=len(feature_map.labels),task=task,**kwargs)

                          if spec.get('source')=='item' and spec['type']!='meta']
        self.user_fields=[name for name,spec in feature_map.features.items()
                          if spec.get('source') not in ['item','action'] and spec['type']!='meta']

        self.action_field=next((name for name,spec in feature_map.features.items() if spec.get('source')=='action'),None)

    def _pool(self, weights, values, counts):
        batch, slots, _ = values.shape
        weights = weights.reshape(batch, slots) * counts.to(weights.dtype)
        weighted = (weights.unsqueeze(-1) * values).reshape(batch, 10, 3, self.value_width)
        return weighted.sum(dim=1)

    def forward(self, inputs):
        context, target, values, mask, auxiliary, detail, position_detail, block_detail, curvature_detail, joint_detail, match_counts, match_union = self._represent(inputs)
        batch = values.shape[0]
        if (self.training and self.training_support == 'full') or self.inference_support == 'full':
            # This training path is exactly the incumbent's operator sequence:
            # all 70 rows enter Dice and retain native support gradients.
            all_values, all_counts = self._compress_with_match(values, mask, auxiliary, match_union)
            primary_weights = self._primary_activation(self._interactions(target, all_values))
            all_strata = self._pool_seven(primary_weights, all_values, all_counts)
            uniform = all_strata[:, 0, :]
            values = all_values.reshape(batch, 10, 7, self.value_width)[:, :, :3, :].reshape(
                batch, 30, self.value_width)
            counts = all_counts.reshape(batch, 10, 7)[:, :, :3].reshape(batch, 30)
            primary_strata = all_strata[:, :3, :]
        elif self.training:
            # Folded and unweighted use five unique assignment rows. The
            # compression-only control restores seven BEFORE every scorer
            # operation, isolating compression arithmetic from affine work.
            unique_values, unique_counts = self._compress_unique_support(
                values, mask, auxiliary, match_union)
            if self.training_support == 'compression_only':
                all_values = self._expand_support_rows(unique_values)
                all_counts = self._expand_support_rows(unique_counts.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
                primary_weights = self._primary_activation(self._interactions(target, all_values))
                all_strata = self._pool_seven(primary_weights, all_values, all_counts)
                primary_strata = all_strata[:, :3, :]
            else:
                interactions = self._interactions(target, unique_values)
                if self.training_support == 'folded':
                    primary_weights = self._folded_support_activation(interactions, batch)
                else:
                    # Ablation removes two support copies from every Dice
                    # population. It is not an equivalence-preserving path.
                    primary_weights = self.local_activation(interactions)
                weights = primary_weights.reshape(batch, 10, 5)[:, :, :3].reshape(batch, 30)
                read_values = unique_values.reshape(batch, 10, 5, self.value_width)[:, :, :3, :].reshape(
                    batch, 30, self.value_width)
                read_counts = unique_counts.reshape(batch, 10, 5)[:, :, :3].reshape(batch, 30)
                primary_strata = self._pool(weights, read_values, read_counts)
            uniform = primary_strata[:, 0, :]
            values = unique_values.reshape(batch, 10, 5, self.value_width)[:, :, :3, :].reshape(
                batch, 30, self.value_width)
            counts = unique_counts.reshape(batch, 10, 5)[:, :, :3].reshape(batch, 30)
        else:
            # Pruning is valid only in eval mode. Never change train/eval
            # flags, running buffers, parameters, or the host batch policy.
            if self.inference_support == 'score_pruned':
                # Retain the original compression arithmetic to isolate the
                # effect of reducing scorer GEMM rows from 70 to 30.
                all_values, all_counts = self._compress_with_match(values, mask, auxiliary, match_union)
                values = all_values.reshape(batch, 10, 7, self.value_width)[:, :, :3, :].reshape(
                    batch, 30, self.value_width)
                counts = all_counts.reshape(batch, 10, 7)[:, :, :3].reshape(batch, 30)
            else:
                # The first three assignment rows of seven-row compression
                # are exactly the inherited uniform/feedback assignment.
                values, counts = self._compress_both(values, mask, auxiliary)
            primary_weights = self._primary_activation(self._interactions(target, values))
            primary_strata = self._pool(primary_weights, values, counts)
            uniform = primary_strata[:, 0, :]

        if self.training:
            # Item fields share tables across current target and past events:
            # gate both uses together. Historical action joins this group.
            # Context includes only supplied non-item/non-action features.
            aux_context = context.detach() if self.block_aux_context_grad else context
            aux_target = target.detach() if self.block_aux_item_grad else target
            aux_values = values.detach() if self.block_aux_item_grad else values
            aux_detail = detail.detach() if self.block_aux_item_grad else detail
            aux_position_detail = position_detail.detach() if self.block_aux_item_grad else position_detail
            aux_block_detail = block_detail.detach() if self.block_aux_item_grad else block_detail
            aux_curvature_detail = curvature_detail.detach() if self.block_aux_item_grad else curvature_detail
            aux_joint_detail = joint_detail.detach() if self.block_aux_item_grad else joint_detail
            aux_weights = self._auxiliary_activation(self._interactions(aux_target, aux_values))
            feedback_population_strata = self._pool(aux_weights, aux_values, counts)
            # Execute feedback scoring in every training cell to match work
            # and collect a complete independent running-state trajectory.
            # Primary strata have all support rows in their native moments;
            # detach the entire result to preserve auxiliary source ownership.
            if self.auxiliary_train_population == 'primary':
                aux_strata = primary_strata.detach()
            else:
                aux_strata = feedback_population_strata
        else:
            # The eval factor never changes training operations. Each choice
            # uses only frozen running moments; eval cannot update either set.
            aux_context, aux_target = context, target
            aux_detail = detail
            aux_position_detail = position_detail
            aux_block_detail = block_detail
            aux_curvature_detail = curvature_detail
            aux_joint_detail = joint_detail
            if self.auxiliary_eval_population == 'feedback':
                aux_weights = self._auxiliary_activation(self._interactions(target, values))
                aux_strata = self._pool(aux_weights, values, counts)
            else:
                aux_strata = primary_strata
        feedback = aux_strata[:, 1, :] + aux_strata[:, 2, :]
        grouped_counts = counts.reshape(counts.shape[0], 10, 3)
        total_count = grouped_counts[:, :, 0].sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
        has_history = (total_count > 0).to(uniform.dtype)
        predictions = {}
        for index, (label, tower) in enumerate(zip(self.feature_map.labels, self.towers)):
            if label == 'is_click':
                task_context, task_target, base = context, target, uniform
                task_detail = detail
                task_position_detail = position_detail
                task_block_detail = block_detail
                task_curvature_detail = curvature_detail
                task_joint_detail = joint_detail
            else:
                task_context, task_target, base = aux_context, aux_target, feedback
                task_detail = aux_detail
                task_position_detail = aux_position_detail
                task_block_detail = aux_block_detail
                task_curvature_detail = aux_curvature_detail
                task_joint_detail = aux_joint_detail
            # Keep the two uses numerically identical. Detach only the
            # selected context edge; every auxiliary adapter/tower parameter
            # remains in its task loss graph. Eval has no gradient gating.
            adapter_context = task_context
            tower_context = task_context
            if self.training and label != 'is_click':
                if self.block_aux_adapter_context_grad:
                    adapter_context = adapter_context.detach()
                if self.block_aux_tower_context_grad:
                    tower_context = tower_context.detach()
            signal = torch.cat([task_detail, task_position_detail, task_block_detail,
                                task_curvature_detail, task_joint_detail], dim=-1)
            residual_features = torch.cat([adapter_context, task_target, base,
                                           match_counts.to(base.dtype), signal], dim=-1)
            # Task routing is required by __init__. Each adapter still
            # receives its own task's features once; every parameter remains
            # in the loss graph. Unselected adapters are stateless and their
            # outputs have zero loss derivative in the all-bank control.
            if self.residual_execution == 'direct':
                correction = self.residual_bank[index](residual_features)
            else:
                bank = torch.stack([adapter(residual_features)
                                    for adapter in self.residual_bank], dim=1)
                correction = bank[:, index, :] if self.residual_routing == 'task' else bank.mean(dim=1)
            pooled = base + has_history * correction
            features = torch.cat([tower_context, task_target, pooled], dim=-1)
            predictions[label + '_pred'] = torch.sigmoid(tower(features))
        return predictions

251: Among all those features of Table 1, user behavior features are critically important and play key roles in modeling user interests in the scenario of e-commerce applications.
252: Base model obtains a fixed-length representation vector of user interests by pooling all the embedding vectors over the user behavior feature group, as Eq.(1). This representation vector stays the same for a given user, in regardless of what candidate ads are.
253: In this way, the user representation vector with a limited dimension will be a bottleneck to express user’s diverse interests.
254: To make it capable enough, an easy method is to expand the dimension of embedding vector, which unfortunately will increase the size of learning parameters heavily.
255: It will lead to overfitting under limited training data and add the burden of computation and storage, which may not be tolerated for an industrial online system.
256: Is there an elegant way to represent user’s diverse interests in one vector under limited dimension?
257: The local activation characteristic of user interests gives us inspiration to design a novel model named deep interest network(DIN).
258: Imagine when the young mother mentioned above in section 3 visits the e-commerce site, she finds the displayed new handbag cute and clicks it.
259: Let’s dissect the driving force of click action.
260: The displayed ad hits the related interests of this young mother by soft-searching her historical behaviors and finding that she had browsed similar goods of tote bag and leather handbag recently.

262: DIN simulates this process by paying attention to the representation of locally activated interests w.r.t. given ad.
263: Instead of expressing all user’s diverse interests with the same vector, DIN adaptively calculate the representation vector of user interests by taking into consideration the relevance of historical behaviors w.r.t. candidate ad.

285: In the advertising system in Alibaba, numbers of goods and users scale up to hundreds of millions.
286: Practically, training industrial deep networks with large scale sparse input features is of great challenge.

337: 6. Experiments
338: In this section, we present our experiments in detail, including datasets, evaluation metric, experimental setup, model comparison and the corresponding analysis.
339: Experiments on two public datasets with user behaviors as well as a dataset collected from the display advertising system in Alibaba demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed approach which outperforms state-of-the-art methods on the CTR prediction task.
340: Both the public datasets and experiment codes are made available1.
341: 6.1. Datasets and Experimental Setup
342: Amazon Dataset22
343: 2
344: http://jmcauley.ucsd.edu/data/amazon/.
345: Amazon Dataset contains product reviews and metadata from Amazon, which is used as benchmark dataset(He and McAuley, 2016; Mcauley
346: et al., ; Veit
347: et al., 2015). We conduct experiments on a subset named Electronics, which contains 192,403 users, 63,001 goods, 801 categories and 1,689,188 samples. User behaviors in this dataset are rich, with more than 5 reviews for each users and goods. Features include goods_id, cate_id, user reviewed goods_id_list and cate_id_list. Let all behaviors of a user be (b1,b2,…,bk,…,bnb_{1},b_{2},\ldots,b_{k},\ldots,b_{n}), the task is to predict the (k+1)-th reviewed goods by making use of the first k reviewed goods.
348: Training dataset is generated with k=1,2,…,n−2k=1,2,\ldots,n-2 for each user. In the test set, we predict the last one given the first n−1n-1 reviewed goods.
349: For all models, we use SGD as the optimizer with exponential decay, in which learning rate starts at 1 and decay rate is set to 0.1. The mini-batch size is set to be 3232.
350: MovieLens Dataset33
351: 3
352: https://grouplens.org/datasets/movielens/20m/. MovieLens data(Harper and
353: Konstan, 2015) contains 138,493 users, 27,278 movies, 21 categories and 20,000,263 samples. To make it suitable for CTR prediction task, we transform it into a binary classification data. Original user rating of the movies is continuous value ranging from 0 to 5. We label the samples with rating of 4 and 5 to be positive and the rest to be negative. We segment the data into training and testing dataset based on userID. Among all 138,493 users, of which 100,000 are randomly selected into training set (about 14,470,000 samples) and the rest 38,493 into the test set (about 5,530,000 samples). The task is to predict whether user will rate a given movie to be above 3(positive label) based on historical behaviors. Features include movie_id, movie_cate_id and user rated movie_id_list, movie_cate_id_list. We use the same optimizer, learning rate and mini-batch size as described on Amazon Dataset.
354: Alibaba Dataset. We collected traffic logs from the online display advertising system in Alibaba, of which two weeks’ samples are used for training and samples of the following day for testing. The size of training and testing set is about 2 billions and 0.14 billion respectively. For all the deep models, the dimensionality of embedding vector is 12 for the whole 16 groups of features. Layers of MLP is set by 192×200×80×2192\times 200\times 80\times 2. Due to the huge size of data, we set the mini-batch size to be 5000 and use Adam(Kingma and Ba, 2015) as the optimizer. We apply exponential decay, in which learning rate starts at 0.001 and decay rate is set to 0.9.
355: The statistics of all the above datasets is shown in Table 2.
356: Volume of Alibaba Dataset is much larger than both Amazon and MovieLens, which brings more challenges.

Training with fine-grained g​o​o​d​s​_​i​d​sgoods\_ids features without regularization encounters serious overfitting after the first epoch. All the regularizations show improvement, among which our proposed mini-batch aware regularization performs best. Besides, well trained model with g​o​o​d​s​_​i​d​sgoods\_ids features gets higher AUC than without them. It comes from the richer information that fine-grained features contained.
381: 6.2. Competitors
382: •
383: LR(Mcmahan
384: et al., 2014). Logistic regression (LR) is a widely used shallow model before deep networks for CTR prediction task. We implement it as a weak baseline.
385: •
386: BaseModel. As introduced in section4.2, BaseModel follows the Embedding&MLP architecture and is the base of most of subsequently developed deep networks for CTR modeling. It acts as a strong baseline for our model comparison.
387: •
388: Wide&Deep(et al., 2016a).
389: In real industrial applications, Wide&Deep model has been widely accepted.
390: It consists of two parts: i) wide model, which handles the manually designed cross product features, ii) deep model, which automatically extracts nonlinear relations among features and equals to the BaseModel.
391: Wide&Deep needs expertise feature engineering on the input of the "wide" module.
392: We follow the practice in (Guo
393: et al., 2017) to take cross-product of user behaviors and candidates as wide inputs.
394: For example, in MovieLens dataset, it refers to the cross-product of user rated movies and candidate movies."

item.text: The evidence points to a narrower question: auxiliary feedback helped click prediction through the context input to the history adapter, but the combined result does not show which task supplied that benefit. I’ll prepare a four-way comparison that independently enables context gradients from cart/favorite tasks and purchase tasks. All four models will retain the same inputs, parameters, forward calculations, normalization, and losses.
